title: Reducing Oxygen Toxicity in Very Preterm Infants through Physiologically Based Cord Clamping (PBCC) Compared to Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC): A Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial on Cumulative Oxygen Exposure in the First 10 Minutes of Life
summary: This study investigates whether preterm infants (born between 28+0 and 32+0 weeks of gestation) experience less oxygen-related damage if they are stabilized while still attached to the umbilical cord (PBCC) compared to the standard method of delayed cord clamping (DCC). The goal is to reduce the total amount of oxygen needed during the first minutes of life.

interventions.name: Physiologically Based Cord Clamping (PBCC) – Neonatal stabilization at the intact umbilical cord using the Concord Birth Trolley®
Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) – Clamping after 30–60 seconds followed by standard neonatal care in a separate resuscitation area

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preterm infants with gestational age between 28+0 and 32+0 weeks
Written informed consent from legal guardians obtained before delivery
Exclusion criteria:
Preterm or newborn infants with major congenital malformations affecting:
respiratory regulation (e.g., severe CNS malformations),
lung function (e.g., pulmonary hypoplasia, diaphragmatic hernia),
or cardiovascular function (e.g., cyanotic congenital heart defects)
Lack of parental consent prior to delivery
